notes.summary: A series question gives terms that follow a pattern and asks for the next or missing term. SSC asks 2–4 questions: number, letter and mixed (alphanumeric) series.

concepts.title: Differences first
concepts.body: Write the difference between terms. If the differences form a pattern (same, +2 each time, squares 1, 4, 9 …), you have the rule.

concepts.title: Multiply-add patterns
concepts.body: If terms grow fast, try ×2, ×3, or ×2 + 1. Example: 3, 7, 15, 31 → each term ×2 + 1.

concepts.title: Letter and mixed series
concepts.body: Change letters to positions (A=1 … Z=26) and treat each part (letter, number, letter) as its own series.

varieties.name: Number series
varieties.how: Check differences, then ratios, then ×a + b.

varieties.name: Letter series
varieties.how: Convert to positions and find the step.

varieties.name: Alphanumeric series
varieties.how: Split each term into parts and solve each part separately.

steps: First letters A, C, E: +2 → G
Last letters Z, X, V: −2 → T

tips: If differences are not equal, take differences of differences.
Squares (1, 4, 9, 16, 25) and cubes appear often in differences.
For letter series, remember EJOTY: E=5, J=10, O=15, T=20, Y=25.
traps: Do not stop at the first rule that fits two terms; check it on every term.
In mixed series, letters and numbers usually follow different rules.

questions.q:
Select the number that will come next in the following series.
2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?

Select the letter that will come next in the series.
B, E, H, K, ?

Select the number that will come next.
3, 7, 15, 31, 63, ?

Select the letter-cluster that will come next.
AZ, BY, CX, ?
questions.solution:
First letters: A, B, C → D (+1).
Second letters: Z, Y, X → W (−1).
Answer: DW.

questions.q:
Select the number that will come next.
1, 2, 6, 15, 31, ?

Select the term that will come next.
A1Z, C3X, E5V, G7T, ?
questions.solution:
First letters: A, C, E, G → I (+2).
Numbers: 1, 3, 5, 7 → 9.
Last letters: Z, X, V, T → R (−2).
Answer: I9R.

flashcards.back: Squares: the next difference is the next square
